correctness.rationale: Partial fractions of the moment-generating function give the exact interior tail formula. At r=0 its expansion has quadratic coefficient 1-t/sqrt(2), proving the sparse local-type switch. Around equal weights, writing p=1/2+q makes the q^2 coefficient proportional to h'''(1/2), whose sign is exactly 4t^2-6t-3, giving the stated positive root. The endpoint ratio is (1+t) exp(-(2-sqrt(2))t); its log derivative has one maximum and is strictly decreasing through the relevant interval, giving one further positive crossing and the Lambert-W expression. Independent numerical/algebraic checks reproduce t_*=1.687952825208936 between sqrt(2) and 1.895643923738960. Compactness plus strict local maximality of both endpoints forces an interior global minimum. No claim of uniqueness is used.

final_claim: For two independent standard Laplace variables with nonnegative weights of fixed squared norm one, the sparse endpoint changes local type at t=sqrt(2), the equal-weight endpoint changes local type at t=(3+sqrt(21))/4, and their tail heights have exactly one positive crossover t_* given by the stated Lambert-W formula, with sqrt(2)<t_*<(3+sqrt(21))/4; throughout the intervening coexistence window both endpoints are strict local maxima and at least one global minimizer is interior.
